title: The 10 Best Car Ramps
subtitle: Plastic car ramps for oil changes and under-car maintenance, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: Car ramps lift the front of your car in seconds so you can change the oil or inspect underneath without a jack. We ranked 10 best-sellers from Ironton, MaxxHaul, ROBLOCK, TOWKING and others on rating, review volume and features (6 inches or more of lift, a gentle incline, rubber feet, stackable storage and a matched pair).

avoid.name: VEVOR Car Ramps, 2 PCS, 13,000 lb GVW, 6.3-Inch Lift (TS295DT)
avoid.flag: Listing contradicts itself on capacity and lift
avoid.verdict: A ramp set whose listing gives two different lift heights and a capacity that doesn't add up, on a product you'll lie under.
reasons: The title says 6.3-inch lift, but the bullets say 6.7 inches, and the part number field reads 'Car ramps,6.3 in lift', a description rather than a part number.
The title says 13,000 lb GVW, but the bullets say 4,000 lb per ramp and 8,000 lb per pair, which works out to 16,000 lb GVW on other brands' math.
It's rated 4.3 stars and costs over $100. The Ironton set is about $59, rated 4.7, and states 6,000 lb per ramp plainly.

buyers_guide.q: How much capacity do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Check your vehicle's curb weight. Ramps hold one end, so a pair rated at your curb weight or more covers it. Ratings are given per ramp, per pair or as GVW; read which one the number means.
6 to 7 inches is enough for an oil change on most cars. Trucks and SUVs benefit from 7 inches or more.
Look for a gentle incline (17 degrees or less) or long ramps like the MaxxHaul 50709. Very low cars can use short jack-assist ramps to get a floor jack under them.
Good polypropylene honeycomb ramps are rated for heavy loads and won't rust. Use them on flat, hard ground, set the parking brake and chock the rear wheels.
Ramps are faster for oil changes. Jack stands are needed when the wheels must come off or hang free.
